# Clean Environment.
Honest budgets.
Accountable leadership.
Three years of doing what a water board director should do — asking hard questions, holding the line on rates, and making sure Ward 7 has a voice at EBMUD.

Castro Valley Forum · August 2023
## “EBMUD Director Calls for More Oversight”
$279 million moved between projects with no approval or visibility from the elected board. April asked where the money went — and the reforms followed.
“That’s a lot of money going project to project, and directors have no idea about it.”
April Chan, to the Castro Valley Forum
Fire safety is on the ballot.Firefighters asked April for accountability from EBMUD. She delivered EBMUD’s first-ever fire hydrant inspection standard.
Keep the water flowing →
The choice
## Who’s watching your water money?
### April Chan
- Helped expose $279 million in out-of-view budget transfers, then pushed through the reforms
- Voted to cap rate increases at 6.5%
- Voted to end the 8% drought surcharge
- Delivered EBMUD’s first fire hydrant inspection standard
### Her opponent’s record on your bills
He ran an agency funded mostly by East Bay garbage bills. A civil grand jury found those bills had risen about 70%. He was paid $213,000 a year plus benefits and, the Chronicle reported, felt he should have gotten an even bigger raise. He didn’t return the paper’s calls.
Source: Matier & Ross, San Francisco Chronicle, 2011
Hear him explain the 36% increase in his own words →
Experience running agencies isn’t the same as watching your bill.
How to vote ↓ Join the Team
Your ballot is on its way
## When and how to vote
Every registered voter gets a ballot by mail. Fire safety is on the ballot. Look near the end for April in the East Bay Municipal Utility District, Ward 7 contest. She’s the 2nd name.
- Oct 5Ballots start arrivingCounties begin mailing ballots, and 24-hour drop boxes open.
- Oct 19Last day to register onlineMissed it? You can still register and vote in person at a vote center through Election Day.
- Nov 3Election DayMailed ballots must be postmarked by November 3. Drop boxes and vote centers close at 8 p.m.
Register or check your status Find a drop box Compare the candidates on VOTE411
Where April Stands
## Three priorities. One record to back them up.
Not talking points — things April has already delivered on the board.
### Affordable Rates
Voted to cap rate increases at 6.5% and eliminated the 8% drought surcharge when the drought ended. Fighting to keep water affordable for every Ward 7 family.
See the record →
### Accountability & Transparency
Raised concerns that helped bring $279 million in out-of-view budget transfers to light — then pushed through reforms. You deserve to know how every dollar is spent.
See the record →
### Clean Environment
Stopped soil dumping on Lake Chabot Road. Held the line against projects that would harm our community and our watershed.

Why She Ran
## No issue is more important for California than water.
When April ran for EBMUD in 2022, California was coming off a multi-year severe drought. She saw a board that needed fresh perspective, direct community engagement, and a willingness to ask hard questions.
She ran — and won — because she believed the people of Ward 7 deserved a director who would show up, listen, and fight for their interests.
Three years later, she has a record to prove it.
Read her full story →
Rooted at Home
## Fairview is home. Water is personal.
April lives in Fairview with her husband Dexter and their son Kai. The water she works to protect is the water her family drinks — and the water the next generation will depend on.
She has represented Ward 7 as an elected EBMUD Director since 2023.
That is the standard behind every vote she takes on the EBMUD Board.
Record of Results
## What April has delivered in her first term.
✓
#### Established EBMUD’s first-ever fire hydrant inspection standard
Firefighters asked April for accountability from EBMUD. She delivered the District’s first hydrant inspection standard, supported by firefighters. Fire safety is on the ballot →
✓
#### Stopped soil dumping on Lake Chabot Road
Blocked a project that would have sent 100 trucks a day through San Leandro and Castro Valley. Over 1,500 Ward 7 residents signed petitions alongside her — material redirected to Delta levee improvements.
✓
#### Helped expose $279 million in out-of-view budget transfers
Elevated constituent concerns to EBMUD’s internal auditor — staff had been moving funds between capital projects without public visibility. Pushed through reforms so it can’t happen again.
✓
#### Voted to cap rate increases at 6.5%
Kept water affordable for East Bay families. Eliminated the 8% drought surcharge when the drought ended — money back in your pocket.
✓
#### Voted against Redwood Road soil importation
The material contained asphalt, concrete, and pipeline debris — a violation of the principles of the 2019 Soil Importation Ordinance April helped establish on the Fairview Municipal Advisory Council.
Questions about the 2025 investigation? Read the facts, with sources →

## Meeting neighbors in Bay-O-Vista
On October 4, 2026, neighbors in San Leandro’s Bay-O-Vista neighborhood hosted a meet and greet for April. Four guests recorded video endorsements for her at the event.
### Video endorsements from the meet and greet
Kat WellmanBay-O-Vista resident · 1:14 Read the transcript
My name is Kat Wellman. I actually live in Bay-O-Vista and have been very involved in community activism. And I have to say that April Chan is probably the best elected representative for her constituents that I have ever met. Four years ago, we were facing East Bay MUD, actually wanting to take all of its extracted soil and put it into the quarry site, which is our open hillsides here in San Leandro. It would have ruined our community. It would have ruined two other nearby communities and actually made a devastation of our freeways. And it was April’s very first East Bay MUD meeting where she was there when we protested and she came out to the lobby and she represented us and told us that she was going to fight with us and did it the entire time. She is also working now to actually make sure that we are fire safe. She’s having East Bay MUD accountable for checking to make sure we have water in our hydrants. I urge everybody to vote for April Chan for East Bay MUD. You will not find anybody else that would represent the constituents as well as she does. Thank you.
Watch on YouTube (opens in a new tab)
Eric HonSan Leandro resident · 1:22 Read the transcript
I’m here as a constituent of San Leandro. I am here to show my support for April Chan. She’s been instrumental in making a difference in our community in San Leandro and in all of the areas that she’s serving. In particular, there was an incident a couple years ago where there was East Bay MUD who was trying to dump truckloads of dirt into the San Leandro quarry for the next 50 years. And it would have been a disaster for the whole community. She was the one person that stood up with our community to push back against East Bay MUD. And when all the odds were against us, she is a hero. She championed the whole program. And then on top of that, she was the difference maker that made it so that we were able to eventually defer that project away from the community, protect our other constituents. And I hope that you guys read up on this situation and find out how important she is to the community, how important it is that we re-elect her and do everything we can to make sure we have strong representation, who cares about constituents, who also has Asian representation, female representation, and she is a wonderful person as well. Thank you.
